title: Gujarat Approves ₹3,400 Crore Rural Road Upgrade
shortDescription: Gujarat sanctioned ₹3,400 crore to resurface over 5,700 km of non-plan roads across all 33 districts, covering roughly two-thirds of such roads statewide.
genZNote: 5,700 km, 33 districts, one number to remember: ₹3,400 crore — that's the whole card.

sections.heading: What Happened
sections.body: On 1 April 2026, the Gujarat government approved ₹3,400 crore for the resurfacing of non-plan roads connecting villages across the state, announced by state spokesperson and minister Jitu Vaghani.

sections.heading: Key Facts
bullets: Over 5,700 km of roads to be resurfaced, across 2,342 individual works.
Coverage spans all 33 districts of Gujarat.
Expected to cover nearly 67% of the state's non-plan (village-connecting) roads.
Aimed at improving connectivity in remote and interior regions.

sections.heading: Why It Matters
sections.body: Rural road connectivity is a recurring theme across Gujarat's development current affairs and ties to broader Indian infrastructure GK (e.g. PMGSY-style rural road schemes at the national level) — this is a state-level example of the same policy priority.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Gujarat approved ₹3,400 crore in April 2026 to resurface over 5,700 km of village-connecting roads across all 33 districts.
keyFacts: Covers ~67% of the state's non-plan roads.
commonConfusion: This is a GUJARAT state scheme, not a Union government rural-roads scheme (like PMGSY) — keep the two separate in an MCQ.

highYieldFacts: ₹3,400 crore, 5,700+ km, all 33 districts — the three numbers most likely to be tested together.
commonTraps: Confusing this Gujarat state-funded road scheme with a central government rural-roads programme.
mustRemember: ₹3,400 crore road upgrade = Gujarat, April 2026, 5,700+ km, 33 districts.
